case_name: State Of Haryana And Ors. Etc. Etc. v Piara Singh And Ors. Etc. Etc.
petitioner: State Of Haryana And Ors. Etc. Etc
facts: This batch of Special Leave Petitions are directed against the judgment of a Division Bench of Punjab and Haryana High Court in a batch of writ petitions...

A large number of appointments were made to Class III and IV services in the States of Punjab and Haryana on ad hoc basis i.e., without reference to Public Service Commission or the Subordinate Services Selection Board and without adhering to employment exchange requirements.
Over the last several years a large number of appointments were made to Class III and IV services in the States of Punjab and Haryana on ad hoc basis...
The orders issued by the Government of Punjab are the following: ...
It is this category of people who approached the High Court of Punjab and Haryana praying for issuance of Writ, Order of Direction for regularisation of their service.
Besides the ad hoc/temporary employees, certain other categories of persons also approached the High Court whose cases too have been dealt with in the judgment under appeal.
issues: The conditions prescribed in the orders of regularisation aforementioned, as bad
The requirement that the employee should have been sponsored by employment exchange..
The requirement that the concerned posts should not be within the purview of S.S.S.B.
The principle of continuing employees on adhoc basis for more than one year without regularising them is arbitrary and unreasonable.
petitioner_arguments: There is no magic in fixing a date by which an employee was to complete the prescribed tenure of service for regularisation.......fixing of a date has no reasonable basis or intelligible differentia for the object to achieve......

If at a given moment suitable candidates amongst candidates sponsored by the Employment Exchanges are not available or no candidate has been sponsored by the Employment Exchange and recruitment is made on ad hoc basis from the sources other than employment exchange, it cannot be said in regularisation policy that such candidates would not be entitled to be regularised.

Inasmuch as most of the Class III and Class IV posts were kept out of the purview of the S.S.S.B. in the State of Haryana during the period 1970 to March, 1987 and also because for a period of ten years there was no S.S.S.B. in existence in this State, imposition of this condition by the Government of Haryana is unreasonable and arbitrary.
respondent_arguments: No finding was, however, recorded that the petitioners or any of them were appointed without reference to the Employment Exchange only after the Employment Exchange intimated the concerned authority that no suitable candidate is available with it.
The State Government should avoid making any ad hoc appointments. If they do so, it shall be for initial period of six months and not be extended beyond other six months.

The Punjab State employees covered by Group No. 1 would be considered as regular members of the service on completion of more than one year after ignoring national and permissible breaks in service...
court_reasoning: There is no magic in fixing a date by which an employee was to complete the prescribed tenure of service for regularisation.......fixing of a date has no reasonable basis or intelligible differentia for the object to achieve......

If at a given moment suitable candidates amongst candidates sponsored by the Employment Exchanges are not available or no candidate has been sponsored by the Employment Exchange and recruitment is made on ad hoc basis from the sources other than employment exchange, it cannot be said in regularisation policy that such candidates would not be entitled to be regularised.

Inasmuch as most of the Class III and Class IV posts were kept out of the purview of the S.S.S.B. in the State of Haryana during the period 1970 to March, 1987 and also because for a period of ten years there was no S.S.S.B. in existence in this State, imposition of this condition by the Government of Haryana is unreasonable and arbitrary.
holding: The directions ultimately granted by the High Court while allowing the batch of writ petitions are to the following effect:
(1) The State Government should avoid making any ad hoc appointments.

(2) The Punjab State employees covered by Group No. 1 would be considered as regular members of the service on completion of more than one year after ignoring national and permissible breaks in service...
